title: Kairos: Low-latency Multi-Agent Serving with Shared LLMs and Excessive Loads in the Public Cloud
technique: workflow orchestrator + workflow-aware priority scheduling (by remaining end-to-end workflow latency) + memory-aware time-slot dispatching across LLM instances

optimized_metrics.evidence: We therefore propose Kairos, a multi-agent orchestration system that optimizes end-to-end latency for multi-agent applications.
reduce end-to-end tail latency, Kairos prioritizes requests ... that have already experienced longer delays in prior stages.
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: P90 tail latency decrease ranging from 19.1% to 28.6%

optimized_metrics.evidence: The scheduler decides the serving priority of the requests based on their latency characteristics to reduce the overall queuing.

headline_claim.text: Kairos reduces end-to-end latency by 17.8% to 28.4% compared to state-of-the-art works.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We adopt program-level token latency [37] as the performance metric to measure the end-to-end performance of multi-agent applications. This metric is defined as the end-to-end response time divided by the number of tokens generated, with lower values indicating better performance.
metric_definitions.notes: Normalized program (application) latency in s/token, analogous to NORM_LAT but over the whole multi-agent application (all agents' tokens). Not a per-request TTFT/TPOT. Tail is P90/P95/P99 over applications.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: the remaining execution latency distribution for each agent, which reflects the time required to complete the end-to-end workflow from the current execution stage.
metric_definitions.notes: Scheduler priority key: requests of agents closer to workflow end (shorter remaining latency) served first, an SRPT-like policy at program level.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: the average queueing time ratio (i.e., the ratio of queueing time to end-to-end time) ranges from 0% to 90%
metric_definitions.notes: Used to set load: load swept so queueing ratio is 0-90%.

load_regime: trace-like inter-request interval sampling; load rate adjusted so average queueing-time ratio spans 0% to 90%; co-located multi-application workloads
workloads: three multi-agent applications (QA with math/humanities expert routing, report generation, code generation with HumanEval/MBPP/APPS), co-located mixes
extractor_notes: Latency is program-level (whole multi-agent application) and normalized per generated token; baselines Parrot and Ayo. No TTFT/TPOT or throughput reported. Quality not measured.

tail_audit.metrics: multi-agent workflow E2E latency mean + P90 (tail), design targets accumulated-latency tail
tail_audit.correction: Keep PROGRAM_JCT P90 but replace its evidence (currently 'We report both the average and the tail latency', a reporting quote) with the design quote. Medium/weak: intra-agent priority by cumulative latency is the tail-oriented mechanism.

load_class_quote: we construct the loads according ... to a production-level LLM inference trace [§7.1: trace-derived inter-request intervals, load rate swept via queueing-time ratio 0-90%]
